subject: Hosting evaluation & HIPAA evidence — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@pilgrimhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T13:15:00Z
Subject: Hosting evaluation & HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Hi Sanjay — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from the call
- Pilgrim processes PII + limited PHI (claims + member IDs) for care coordination use cases.
- Traffic: ~300k inference requests/month today, expected to grow 3x in 12 months.
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms p95 for short prompts; occasional batch jobs for nightly scoring.
- Preferred hosting: initially Dedicated capacity; open to Private VPC for stronger isolation if procurement requires.

Compliance asks we noted
- Execute a BAA before any PHI goes to hosted environments.
- Need Redwood’s latest SOC2 Type II report and penetration test summary.
- Pilgrim security team will run the security questionnaire and request evidence for encryption at rest/in transit and key management.

Attachments: I’ve attached our short HIPAA evidence checklist (redwood-hipaa-evidence-checklist.pdf) to make it easy to match docs to your questionnaire. 

Proposed next steps
1) Sanjay/systems team to send the full security questionnaire (you mentioned an XLS) — we’ll map evidence to each line item.
2) Redwood to share SOC2 Type II (redacted) and pen-test summary — I’ve looped in Marissa and Rishi to own evidence mapping.
3) If procurement prefers Dedicated, we’ll prepare a capacity/price estimate and an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP). If Pilgrim requires VPC/on-prem, we’ll surface the deployment checklist and timeline.

Could you confirm target timeline for the procurement decision (2–4 weeks?) and who from your side will be the procurement/security point(s) of contact?

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@pilgrimhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops@pilgrimhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-21T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosting evaluation & HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Thanks Hannah — good notes. Confirming a few details from our side: 

- Yes, we handle claims and membership PHI. BAA is required.
- SOC2 Type II must be provided; we will accept redacted reports but need scope and auditor name.
- Pen test summary ok as long as it includes critical/major findings and remediation status.
- Our security team will send the questionnaire (attached) — sending now (pilgrim-security-questionnaire.xlsx).

On hosting preference: procurement/legal prefers Dedicated capacity with a BAA for production PHI. However, if Redwood can offer Private VPC with customer-managed KMS, that’s a strong plus and may accelerate sign-off — we’ll surface that to legal.

Timeline: procurement aims to complete vendor selection in 3 weeks (target July 12). Primary procurement contact is me; security leads are secops@pilgrimhealth.com (please loop them for all evidence).

Forwarding the questionnaire in a separate email as requested.

— Sanjay
Director, Data Integrations
Pilgrim Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@pilgrimhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosting evaluation & HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Appreciate the details, Sanjay. I’ll take point on evidence mapping once we get your questionnaire. A few clarifying notes from ops and procurement perspective: 

1) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — what procurement likes about this is deterministic throughput and an SLA-backed latency. We can scope a Dedicated estimate that meets your target p95.

2) Private VPC option — supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering, which helps legal. Timeline-wise, VPC setups typically add ~2–4 weeks to the deployment plan vs. hosted/Dedicated. If you need on-prem, that’s a longer project (Q3+).

3) Evidence we’ll prepare immediately
   - SOC2 Type II (redacted) — will share auditor and scope.
   - Pen test executive summary and remediation timeline.
   - Encryption at rest/in transit whitepaper + key management integration notes.
   - BAA template for legal review.

4) MAP draft: I’ll attach a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for timeline/owners — aim to get a signed MAP to align procurement and security deliverables. 

Hannah — I’ll need the questionnaire by end of day tomorrow to hit Pilgrim’s 3-week window. Sanjay — let me know if weekday evenings are bad for your legal folks; we can change cadence.

Thanks — M

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@pilgrimhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-23T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosting evaluation & HIPAA evidence — post-call recap

Looping in a short technical checklist so Pilgrim security has clear expectations on evidence and configuration options. I’ve also attached a draft MAP (mutual-action-plan-draft.docx) to reflect these items. 

Technical evidence checklist (what we can provide immediately)
- SOC2 Type II (redacted PDF) — includes auditor, report period, and scope.
- Penetration test executive summary (last 12 months) — high-level findings + remediation status.
- Architecture diagram showing Dedicated vs Private VPC topology (we’ll produce on request).
- KMS integration notes: customer-managed keys supported via AWS KMS or Cloud HSM for Private VPC; hosted Dedicated uses Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption.
- Audit logging details: retention windows, access controls, and how logs are exported (CloudWatch/S3).

Recommended immediate asks for Pilgrim security (to accelerate review)
1) Confirm PHI types/fields and whether any data residency constraints apply.
2) Confirm if Pilgrim requires customer-managed KMS in prod — if so, we’ll prioritize Private VPC docs and a technical kickoff.
3) Provide any mandatory compliance checklists from legal (e.g., specific contract clauses) so we can surface them with our legal team.

If Pilgrim is comfortable with Dedicated + BAA for an initial pilot (non-production or pseudonymized data), we can run an 8-week pilot with pre-agreed SLAs and a fast track to VPC for production. Otherwise, plan ~6–8 weeks to stand up Private VPC + KMS depending on procurement cadence.

I’ll follow up with the SOC2 and pen test redactions today. Hannah/Marissa — recommend we draft the MAP in HubSpot and send a DocuSign link for the BAA once legal confirms language.

Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
